issues.description: The StockIngredient getter name is inconsistent between the template and the solution. The template defines getIngredientName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient in the template uses getIngredientName(), while the solution defines getName() and updates Stock.findStockIngredient accordingly. The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify getter names. This inconsistency in method naming across artifacts can confuse students about which getter name to implement and which name the rest of the code (or tests) expects.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name for the ingredient's name across template, solution, and documentation. Prefer a simple and conventional name (e.g., getName()) and update the template StockIngredient to provide getName(), update any usages in Stock.findStockIngredient to call getName(), and adjust the problem statement to mention the expected getter naming convention.

issues.description: The StockIngredient 'name' property is exposed with different getter identifiers across artifacts: the template repository defines getIngredientName(), while the solution repository defines getName(). The problem statement asks students to 'add getters for all the private fields' but does not prescribe a specific getter name. This divergence means the same conceptual entity (the ingredient's name) is referenced with two different method names, which can confuse students when mapping the problem description to the provided template and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent getter name for the StockIngredient name field across template and solution. For example, rename the template's getIngredientName() to getName(), and update all references (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) accordingly — or alternatively change the solution to use getIngredientName() everywhere. Prefer using getName() to match common Java conventions.
